summary: Records the IETF consensus that no update was needed to the IDNA character rules in RFC 5892 when Unicode 6.0 came out. Only three code points from Unicode 5.2 had changed property values, and the rules still held.

plainLanguage.summary: Unicode 6.0 changed character categories for three code points used by IDNA rules. The IETF concluded that these changes did not require an update to RFC 5892.

questions: which code points changed idna properties
did unicode 6.0 require an update to rfc 5892
subtitle: IETF consensus on Unicode 6.0 character changes and IDNA derived properties.

tldr.problem: Unicode 6.0 changed character categories for three code points, which changed their derived IDNA property values under RFC 5892.
tldr.mechanism: The memo records the IETF's assessment of those three property changes and updates the relevant IANA registry.
tldr.outcome: The IETF concluded that Unicode 6.0 did not require an update to RFC 5892.

facts.label: IETF consensus
facts.value: No update to RFC 5892 needed for Unicode 6.0

today: RFC 6452 is a Standards Track document. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Unicode Changes Affect IDNA Properties
sections.content:
RFC 5892 derives properties used to determine how code points are treated in Internationalized Domain Names for Applications (IDNA). When Unicode 6.0 changed the general category of three code points that existed in Unicode 5.2 or earlier, their derived IDNA property values changed too.

The affected code points are U+0CF1, U+0CF2 and U+19DA.
sections.plainLanguage: IDNA rules use character properties from Unicode. A change to a character's Unicode category can change how the IDNA rules treat it.

sections.title: The Three Changed Code Points
sections.content: U+0CF1 (Kannada Sign Jihvamuliya) and U+0CF2 (Kannada Sign Upadhmaniya) changed category from So to Lo, changing their derived property from DISALLOWED to PVALID. U+19DA (New Tai Lue Tham Digit One) changed category from Nd to No, changing its derived property from PVALID to DISALLOWED.
sections.plainLanguage: Two Kannada signs changed from disallowed to valid under the derived IDNA property. One New Tai Lue digit changed from valid to disallowed.

sections.title: IETF Decision and Registry Update
sections.content:
The IETF consensus is that Unicode 6.0's changes do not require an update to RFC 5892. The memo says this conclusion does not rule out changes after future Unicode updates. IANA updated the derived property value registry according to RFC 5892 and Unicode 6.0.

The RFC says the three code points are unlikely to occur in internationalized domain names, so it considers the security implications of these changes minor.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF decided that RFC 5892 did not need to change for Unicode 6.0. The memo does not decide what future Unicode changes may require.
